title: Sworn by the angels who pull souls out hard.
subtitle: The first oath: a difficult death

row.title: death is a handover
sub: by those who can also return it

then: Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas and others said these are {idea}the angels who remove the souls of the children of Adam.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says some souls are taken with difficulty, as if drowning. The surah introduction notes: the angels who take the soul today can restore it tomorrow.
now: A hospital corridor at night. A family waiting outside a room. Death feels like a door slamming shut. {idea}The surah opens by reminding you that someone is sent to open that door{/idea}, and how they open it depends on the life behind it.
old: Death just happens to the body, and that is all.
new: Death is carried out by angels on command, and how it goes is tied to how I lived.
try: Make a short dua today for an easy death and a good ending.

title: And by those who draw souls out gently.
subtitle: The second oath: an easy death
then: Ibn Kathir explains, from Ibn Abbas, that some souls {reward}the angels remove with ease, as if untying them,{/reward} because of their briskness. The two oaths together show two very different departures.
now: You have heard people say of a relative, "She passed so peacefully." You have heard the opposite too. {idea}The verse places that difference in the soul,{/idea} not only in the medical chart.
old: How someone dies is just a matter of their illness.
new: There is a gentle taking and a hard one, and I can live toward the gentle one.
try: Do one thing today you would be glad to have done if it were your last day.

title: By those who glide, swimming through the sky.
subtitle: The third oath: angels in motion
then: Ibn Masud said the swimmers {idea}are the angels{/idea}, and similar was reported from Ali, Mujahid, Said bin Jubayr, and Abu Salih. The surah keeps swearing by angels at work to affirm that the Resurrection is coming.
now: You see a quiet sky and think nothing is going on. Meanwhile your own body runs a thousand processes you never notice. {idea}The unseen world is not empty.{/idea} It is full of servants carrying out His commands.
old: If I cannot see it, nothing is going on there.
new: Around me, unseen, angels are moving at His command.
try: Say Subhanallah once today while looking at an empty sky.

title: By those who race ahead to obey.
subtitle: The fourth oath: eagerness
then: Ali, Masruq, Mujahid, Abu Salih, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri said the racers {idea}are the angels.{/idea} The introduction describes them as those who hasten to carry out Allah's commands. Swearing by them is a pledge that what He commands will happen.
now: The adhan goes off on your phone. You think, "Five more minutes," and finish the episode. {idea}The angels sworn by here race to obey.{/idea} You can move one step closer to that speed.
old: I will get to my prayers once I finish this.
new: The best response to Allah's call is to race toward it.
try: At the next adhan, stand up within one minute.

title: By those who arrange affairs by His command.
subtitle: The fifth oath: the managers

row.title: it is managed
sub: and can be ended and remade

then: Ali, Mujahid, Ata and others said these {idea}are the angels.{/idea} Al-Hasan added that they control affairs from heaven to earth by their Lord's command. The introduction explains: those who run the universe today can, by the same order, end it and bring a new one.
now: Your rent, the bus timetable, the weather forecast, a stranger's kindness at the right moment. It all feels like systems. {idea}Behind the systems is a command.{/idea} Nothing in your life is unmanaged.
old: The world is just running on its own machinery.
new: Every affair is arranged by His command, so the order can change when He wills.
try: Hand one worry to Allah in dua tonight, trusting He arranges it.

title: The first blast shakes everything.
subtitle: What the oaths were sworn for
then: Ibn Abbas said this is {trap}the first of the two blasts of the Horn.{/trap} Mujahid linked it to the Day the earth and mountains shake. The introduction says one jolt is enough to upset the whole system of the world.
now: You have felt a small earthquake, or a building shake as a truck passed. Your heart jumped and everyone stopped talking. {idea}One blast will do that to everything at once.{/idea}
old: The world is too big and stable to end suddenly.
new: It takes only one blast, and everything shakes.
try: Next time something jolts you, a bump or a loud noise, remember this verse.

title: And the second blast follows it.
subtitle: The one that brings everyone back
then: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan and Qatadah explained these as {idea}the first and the second blast.{/idea} Mujahid linked the second to the earth and mountains crushed with one crushing. The introduction says a second jolt brings people out living into a new world.
now: A power cut, the house goes dark, and then a click and everything comes back on. You do not doubt it can happen. {idea}The One who ends it all can switch it all back on.{/idea}
old: When it ends, it ends.
new: The end is followed at once by a beginning.
try: When you wake tomorrow, say the morning dua thanking Allah for bringing you back.

title: Hearts that Day will be pounding.
subtitle: Fear inside
then: Ibn Abbas said the hearts will be {trap}afraid{/trap}, and Mujahid and Qatadah said the same. The introduction notes these are the same people who used to deny the Day, now seeing what they thought impossible.
now: Remember the night before a big exam you had not prepared for. The thumping chest, the dry mouth. {idea}A small version of that is a gift{/idea}: it can push you to prepare while you still can.
old: I do not need to fear something that may never happen.
new: A little fear now is far better than a pounding heart then.
try: Pick one thing that would make you calmer on that Day and start it this week.

title: Their eyes lowered in humiliation.
subtitle: Fear outside

key.label: Two ways to lower the gaze

then: Ibn Kathir says the eyes of the people will be {trap}lowly and disgraced from what they witness of terrors.{/trap} Those who looked at the signs with contempt now cannot raise their eyes.
now: You have seen someone caught in a lie, staring at the floor. Or felt it yourself. {idea}Lowering your eyes in humility before Allah now{/idea} is the way to raise them without shame later.
old: Being humble makes me look weak.
new: Humility chosen now spares me humiliation then.
try: In your next prayer, keep your eyes on the place of sujud the whole time.

title: They ask: will we really be brought back?
subtitle: The deniers' question, quoted

row.title: already done once
sub: He made you the first time

then: Ibn Kathir says this is {trap}the idolators of Quraysh and whoever rejects the Hereafter like them.{/trap} Mujahid said the word refers to the graves. They saw coming back after burial as far-fetched.
now: Standing at a graveside, watching the earth go back in, the thought comes uninvited: is that really it? {idea}The verse names the doubt honestly{/idea} and then the surah answers it.
old: Once someone is buried, it is hard to believe they will rise.
new: The doubt is old. The answer is the One who made me from nothing.
try: Next time you pass a graveyard, say the greeting for its people and remember you will rise.

title: Even after we are hollow, crumbling bones?
subtitle: The doubt gets more specific

row.title: nothing is far
sub: for the One who made it

then: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said the word means {trap}decayed.{/trap} Ibn Abbas described it as a bone so rotten that air enters it. To them, a body that far gone could never come back.
now: You have thrown away a phone so broken that no shop could fix it. That is how we picture old bones. {idea}You are thinking of a repair shop.{/idea} The verse is speaking of the Creator.
old: Some things are broken beyond repair.
new: Nothing is too decayed for the One who created it in the first place.
try: Bring one situation you think is beyond repair to Allah in dua today.

title: Then that would be a losing return, they joke.
subtitle: A sarcastic line that came true
then: Muhammad bin Kab said the Quraysh said: {trap}if Allah brings us back after we die, we will surely be losers.{/trap} It was said as mockery. Yet it shows they knew what such a return would mean for them.
now: Someone jokes, "If there is a Judgement Day, I am finished," and everyone laughs. {idea}Sometimes our jokes say what our hearts already know.{/idea} The better response is to change the ending.
old: It is just a joke. It does not mean anything.
new: When I joke that I would lose, it is a sign to start living so I would not.
try: Notice one thing you joke about to avoid taking it seriously. Take it seriously once.

title: It will take only a single shout.
subtitle: The answer to all their doubts

row.title: one command
sub: like the blink of an eye

then: Ibn Kathir says this is a matter from Allah that {idea}will not occur twice.{/idea} Israfil will blow the Horn and the first and last people will stand before their Lord. He links it to verses saying Allah's command is like the twinkling of an eye.
now: Think of a teacher calling one name across a noisy playground and every child turning around. {idea}Everything they argued about, the graves, the bones, the time, is answered by one call.{/idea}
old: Bringing everyone back would be an impossible project.
new: For Allah it is a single shout, faster than a blink.
try: Next time you blink, remember the Hour is described as faster than that.

title: And suddenly, everyone is awake on open ground.
subtitle: Standing on a new earth
then: Ibn Abbas said the word means {idea}the entire earth{/idea}. Others said its face, or a level place. Ar-Rabi bin Anas pointed to the Day the earth is changed to another earth, one {idea}on which no sin has been done and no blood shed.{/idea}
now: You wake up in a strange hotel room and for a second do not know where you are. Now imagine waking on open ground with all of humanity. {idea}No shelter, no hiding, everyone looking.{/idea}
old: I will have time to get my bearings.
new: One moment in the grave, the next standing wide awake before Allah.
try: Spend one quiet minute today picturing yourself standing there, and what you would want to bring.

title: Have you heard the story of Musa?
subtitle: A story told to the Prophet ﷺ
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah tells His Messenger ﷺ about Musa, sent to Firawn with miracles, while Firawn kept to his disbelief until he was seized. The story is told to show {idea}what happens to those who reject the message,{/idea} and it ends with: a lesson for whoever fears.
now: A friend going through something hard, and you say, "Let me tell you what happened to my uncle." {idea}Stories land where arguments do not.{/idea} The surah pauses its proofs to tell one.
old: Stories of past prophets are history, not about me.
new: The story is told so I can see myself in it before it is too late.
try: Read the story of Musa in this surah, 79:15-26, in one sitting today.

title: His Lord called him in the sacred valley.
subtitle: The moment of the call at Tuwa
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}called out, speaking to him{/idea}, in a purified valley. Tuwa, according to what is correct, is the name of the valley, as mentioned in Surah Ta Ha. The mission begins with a conversation.
now: Before any big step, a new job, a move, a hard conversation, you feel very alone. {reward}Musa's mission began with his Lord speaking to him.{/reward} Your work for good can begin the same way, with you and Allah first.
old: I have to have everything figured out before I start something good.
new: It starts with turning to my Lord and hearing His call.
try: Before your next big decision, pray two rakat and ask Allah for guidance.

title: Go to Firawn. He has crossed every limit.
subtitle: Sent to the most arrogant man
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Firawn {trap}had become haughty, rebellious and arrogant.{/trap} Yet Allah's first instruction to Musa was not to fight him but to go to him with a message.
now: There is someone in your family or office you have written off. Too proud, too far gone. {idea}Allah sent a prophet to Firawn with an invitation.{/idea} Maybe that person still deserves a kind word from you.
old: Some people are too far gone to bother with.
new: Even the most arrogant was first offered a way back.
try: Send one gentle, sincere message to someone you have written off.

title: Would you like to purify yourself?
subtitle: The gentlest possible opening
then: Ibn Kathir explains the question as: {reward}will you respond to the path that will purify you{/reward}, and submit and be obedient? It is phrased as an offer to the most arrogant ruler of his time.
now: You want your brother to quit smoking, or your friend to start praying. You lecture. They shut down. {idea}Musa opened with a question:{/idea} would you like to be clean?
old: To change someone, I need to tell them firmly what they are doing wrong.
new: The best invitation is a gentle offer of something good for them.
try: Rephrase one piece of advice you want to give as a kind question.

title: Let me guide you to your Lord, so you fear Him.
subtitle: Guidance that softens a hard heart
then: Ibn Kathir explains: I will guide you to the worship of your Lord, so that {reward}your heart becomes humble, obedient and submissive to Him{/reward} after it was hard and far from goodness. Notice Musa says your Lord, even to Firawn.
now: You notice your heart has gone hard. Prayers feel mechanical, the news no longer moves you. {idea}The cure offered here is to know your Lord,{/idea} and the right fear comes with that knowing.
old: Fear of Allah is something heavy that makes life gloomy.
new: Knowing my Lord brings a fear that softens my heart and brings me closer to good.
try: Learn the meaning of one of Allah's names today and reflect on it for a minute.

title: Then Musa showed him the greatest sign.
subtitle: Words backed by clear proof
then: Ibn Kathir says Musa showed him, {idea}along with the truthful call, a strong evidence and a clear proof{/idea} that his message was from Allah. Firawn could not say he had not been shown.
now: You ask for a sign before you change. Then the sign comes: a near miss on the road, a friend's sudden death, a prayer answered. {idea}What do you do the day after?{/idea}
old: If I got a clear sign, I would change for sure.
new: Signs come. The test is what I do once I have seen one.
try: Recall one clear sign Allah has shown you. Act on it today in one small way.

title: He saw, he knew, and still he denied.
subtitle: Knowing is not the same as believing
then: Ibn Kathir notes that Firawn's {idea}knowledge that Musa's message was true did not make him a believer.{/idea} Recognition is knowledge of the heart. {reward}Faith is its action:{/reward} complying with the truth and submitting to it.
now: You know smoking harms you, you know you should call your father, you know the prayer time is now. {idea}Knowing is not the problem.{/idea} Faith is the moment knowing turns into doing.
old: I know what is right, so I am basically fine.
new: Knowing the truth only counts when I act on it.
try: Take one thing you know is right and do it today.

title: He turned his back and got busy fighting it.
subtitle: Effort spent against the truth
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Firawn {trap}answered the truth with falsehood{/trap}, gathering the magicians to confront the miracles Musa brought. He was not idle. He worked hard, in the wrong direction.
now: You spend an evening finding articles to prove you were right in an argument you know you lost. {idea}All that effort could have gone into simply saying sorry.{/idea}
old: If I put in enough effort, I can prove I am right.
new: Effort spent fighting the truth is effort wasted.
try: Drop one argument today that you are only continuing to save face.

title: He gathered his people and made a speech.
subtitle: Rallying the crowd
then: After turning away, Firawn {trap}gathered and called out among his people.{/trap} He needed an audience to stand against the truth. The next verse gives his words.
now: When you know you are in the wrong, there is a pull to rally people: a long post, a group chat, "am I wrong here?" {idea}Gathering supporters does not make you right.{/idea}
old: If enough people agree with me, I must be right.
new: Rallying a crowd is often a sign I am running from the truth.
try: Before you seek support for your side of a dispute, ask yourself honestly if you are wrong.

title: I am your lord, the most high.
subtitle: Arrogance at its peak

row.title: I know no god but me
I am your lord most high
my way is the only way

then: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said Firawn said this {trap}after his earlier claim, "I have not known any god for you other than me."{/trap} Arrogance that went unchecked grew into the worst claim a person can make.
now: None of us would say Firawn's words. But at home, at work, in a small team, you can act like the final word. {idea}Arrogance grows in small kingdoms too.{/idea}
old: Firawn's arrogance has nothing to do with someone like me.
new: Every unchecked "I know best" is a small step on his road.
try: Let someone else make one decision today that you would normally control.

title: Allah seized him, an example in both worlds.
subtitle: The end of the self-made lord

row.title: Allah
sub: in this life and the next

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {trap}made an example and admonition of him{/trap} for those like him, in this world and on the Day of Resurrection. He links it to verses about a curse followed by another, and leaders inviting to the Fire.
now: You have watched powerful people fall: a boss, a celebrity, someone who seemed untouchable. {idea}The lesson is not about them.{/idea} It is about how fragile any power in your own hands is.
old: Power and status protect a person.
new: Anyone who forgets they are a servant can be seized in a moment.
try: Use one bit of influence you have today to help someone with less.

title: In this is a lesson for anyone who fears.
subtitle: Who the story is for
then: Ibn Kathir says the story shows the end of {trap}whoever opposes the Messenger ﷺ and rejects his message.{/trap} The lesson is for whoever fears. The people of Makkah were hearing it while doing the same as Firawn.
now: Two people watch the same documentary about a fallen tyrant. One shrugs. One goes quiet and thinks about his own pride. {idea}The lesson is there for both. Only one takes it.{/idea}
old: Stories like this are for bad people.
new: The story is a lesson for anyone with enough fear of Allah to see themselves in it.
try: Ask yourself: which trait of Firawn do I most need to watch in myself?

title: Are you harder to create, or the sky?
subtitle: One question that answers the doubt
then: After the story, the surah returns to the deniers' doubt about being brought back. Ibn Kathir says the answer is plain: {idea}the heaven is more difficult to create than you.{/idea} He links it to verses saying the heavens and earth are greater than the creation of people.
now: You worry whether you can be forgiven, or whether things can be fixed. Then you look up at the night sky over the parking lot. {idea}The One who built that is not stretched by you.{/idea}
old: My situation is too complicated even for Allah.
new: If He built the sky, nothing about me is hard for Him.
try: Look at the sky once today and say: You made this, You can mend me.

title: He raised its ceiling high and made it even.
subtitle: Precision in the sky
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah {idea}made it a lofty structure, vast in its space, with equal sides,{/idea} adorned with stars at night. The listeners in Makkah saw that sky every night without a single light to block it.
now: An architect friend shows you a building and talks about load, balance, proportion. You leave impressed. {idea}The ceiling over every city on earth was proportioned by Allah.{/idea}
old: The sky is just there, nothing to think about.
new: The sky is raised and balanced, a building that points to its Builder.
try: Look up at night this week and find one star. Say SubhanAllah.

title: He darkened its night and brought out its morning.
subtitle: Night and day, both from Him
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}made its night dark and extremely black, and its day bright, luminous and clear.{/idea} Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah and others explained the word as making it dark.
now: A long, bad night: a sick child, a worry that will not stop. Then the window turns grey, then light. {reward}The morning was brought out for you{/reward}, like it is every day.
old: Dark times last forever.
new: The One who darkens the night is the One who brings out the morning.
try: Tomorrow, catch the first light of morning and thank Allah for it.

title: After that, He spread out the earth.
subtitle: The ground made ready for life
then: Ibn Kathir notes that the earth was created before the heaven, but {idea}spread out after the heaven was created.{/idea} Spreading it means He brought out what was inside it. This was said by Ibn Abbas and preferred by Ibn Jarir.
now: You unroll a picnic blanket and lay out the food. Everything ready before anyone sits. {reward}The earth was spread and stocked before you arrived{/reward}.
old: The earth is just where I happen to live.
new: It was spread out and prepared, which means I was expected.
try: Walk outside barefoot for a minute, if you can, and thank Allah for the ground.

title: He brought out its water and its pasture.
subtitle: What came out of the ground
then: Ibn Kathir explains this as what spreading the earth means: {reward}He caused its springs to gush and brought forth its hidden benefits.{/reward} For people of the desert, a spring or green pasture meant survival.
now: You turn on the tap and water just comes. You never think of the wells, the rivers, the rain far away. {idea}Every glass is water He brought out of the earth.{/idea}
old: Water and food are just there, provided by the system.
new: Allah brought them out of the earth for me.
try: Use a little less water today, and thank Allah for every drop.

title: And He set the mountains firm.
subtitle: Anchored in their places
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}settled them, made them firm, and established them in their places.{/idea} He adds that Allah is the Most Wise, the All-Knowing, {reward}Most Kind to His creation, Most Merciful.{/reward}
now: When your life shakes, a lost job, a hard diagnosis, you look for something steady. {reward}The One who fixed the mountains firm is the One you can lean on.{/reward}
old: Nothing in my life feels stable.
new: The One who anchored the mountains can anchor my heart.
try: When something shakes you today, say Hasbunallahu wa nimal wakil.

title: All of it as provision for you and your animals.
subtitle: Who the earth was prepared for
then: Ibn Kathir says all this was done {reward}as provision and benefit for you and your cattle.{/reward} For a people who lived by their herds, the point was clear. The next verse turns straight to the Great Catastrophe.
now: Your groceries, your pet's food, the milk in the fridge. All of it traces back to this verse. {idea}A gift this large is not given without a question later{/idea}: what did you do with it?
old: I paid for my food, so it is mine.
new: It is provision prepared for me by Allah, and I will be asked about it.
try: Share one meal or some food with someone today.

title: When the Great Catastrophe finally comes.
subtitle: The event that overcomes everything
then: Ibn Abbas said this is {trap}the Day of Judgement{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says it is called this because {trap}it will overcome every matter.{/trap} The surah has finished its proofs. Now it describes what happens when the Day comes.
now: A deadline, a fight with your spouse, a flight delay. Each one feels like the biggest problem in the world. {idea}The verse gives you a sense of scale.{/idea} Most of today's crises will look small next to that Day.
old: My current crisis is the most important thing in my life.
new: One event will overshadow all the others, and that changes how I weigh today.
try: Next time something feels huge, ask: will this matter on that Day?

title: The Day you remember everything you strove for.
subtitle: Memory returns in full
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}the son of Adam will reflect on all his deeds, the good and the evil.{/idea} He links it to the verse: on that Day man will remember, but how will remembering help him then?
now: Your phone shows a memory: a photo from five years ago. You had forgotten that whole day. {idea}On that Day nothing is forgotten.{/idea} The best memories to have then are the ones you make now.
old: Most of what I do slips from memory and does not matter.
new: I will remember all of it. I would rather remember now, while I can still act.
try: Before sleep, recall today's deeds and seek forgiveness for one.

title: Hell made plain for anyone who can see.
subtitle: No longer hidden
then: Ibn Kathir says it {trap}will become apparent for the onlookers{/trap}, and people will see it with their own eyes. What the deniers called far-fetched will be in plain sight.
now: People say, "I will believe it when I see it." {idea}This verse says that day of seeing is coming for everyone.{/idea} Faith is trusting before the curtain is pulled back, and turning while you can.
old: I will take it seriously when I see real proof.
new: Everyone will see it. The gift is believing before that.
try: Make one choice today based on what you believe about the unseen.

title: As for the one who rebelled.
subtitle: The first of two people
then: Ibn Kathir explains it as {trap}one who rebels and behaves arrogantly.{/trap} The same word was used for Firawn earlier in the surah. Now it is used for anyone, showing Firawn's road is open to ordinary people too.
now: You do not rule a nation. But you might dismiss a parent's advice, ignore a limit, or treat a waiter badly. {idea}The word that described Firawn can describe small moments of yours.{/idea}
old: Rebellion against Allah is what really evil people do.
new: Every arrogant step past a limit is a small rebellion.
try: Notice one moment of arrogance today and correct it with an apology.

title: And put this world ahead of everything.
subtitle: The choice behind the rebellion
then: Ibn Kathir explains that he {trap}gives it precedence over the matters of his religion and his Hereafter.{/trap} The verse does not condemn living in the world. It names putting it first.
now: The meeting runs into prayer time and you let it. The weekend is full and there is no space for Quran. {idea}It is rarely one big choice.{/idea} It is a hundred small moments of putting the world first.
old: I am not choosing the world over Allah. I am just busy.
new: Being too busy for Allah is exactly what preferring this world looks like.
try: Block five minutes in your calendar today just for Allah, and keep it.

title: Then Hell will be his refuge.
subtitle: Where that road ends
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}his final destination will be Hell.{/trap} The word for refuge is the same one used for the believer's Paradise two verses later. The two destinations are set side by side.
now: The verse is short and sober. It is not here to make you despair. {idea}It is a signpost at a fork in the road{/idea}, and you are still standing at the fork.
old: Thinking about Hell only makes me anxious.
new: It is a warning at the fork, while I can still choose the other road.
try: Make sincere tawbah today for one thing, and trust that the door is open.

title: Whoever feared standing before his Lord and held back desire.
subtitle: The second of two people
then: Ibn Kathir explains that he {idea}fears standing before Allah and His judgement{/idea}, he prevents his soul from following its desires, and {reward}compels it to obey its Master.{/reward} It is the exact opposite of the rebel.
now: 11pm. The phone is in your hand and you know what you are about to open. {idea}The verse is about that moment.{/idea} Remembering you will stand before your Lord is what helps you put it down.
old: I cannot help it. My desires are stronger than me.
new: Remembering the standing before my Lord gives me the strength to say no.
try: Choose one desire to hold back today, just once, for the sake of Allah.

title: Then Paradise will be his refuge.
subtitle: Where the other road ends
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}his final abode, destination and place of return will be the spacious Paradise.{/reward} The same word for refuge used two verses earlier now points to the opposite place.
now: You held your tongue in that argument. You skipped the thing you would regret. Nobody saw. {reward}This verse saw.{/reward} Every small no to desire is a step toward a home.
old: Holding back my desires just means missing out.
new: What I hold back for Allah becomes a home in Paradise.
try: Ask Allah tonight for Al-Firdaws, by name.

title: They ask you: when exactly is the Hour?
subtitle: The wrong question
then: People kept asking the Prophet ﷺ to name the time of the Hour. Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}its knowledge is not with him, nor with any creature,{/idea} only with Allah. He links it to the verse that it will come all of a sudden.
now: Videos online counting signs, predicting dates. People who never pray debating the timeline. {idea}Knowing the date would not save anyone.{/idea} Being ready would.
old: If I knew when, I would get ready in time.
new: Not knowing when is the reason to be ready now.
try: Skip one end-times video or debate this week and spend that time on a good deed.

title: What do you have to do with naming its time?
subtitle: Not even the Prophet ﷺ knows

row.title: no one knows
sub: more than the one who asks

then: Ibn Kathir recalls that when Jibril asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the Hour, he said: {idea}the one asked knows no more than the one asking.{/idea} The verse makes clear that naming its time is not part of his role.
now: Someone forwards you a message: "Scholars say it will happen in this year." It spreads through the family group. {idea}If the Prophet ﷺ did not know, no forwarded message does.{/idea}
old: Someone somewhere must know when the end will come.
new: Not even the Prophet ﷺ was given its time. Only Allah knows.
try: If you get a message predicting the Hour, gently do not forward it.

title: Its final knowledge rests with your Lord.
subtitle: Where the question ends
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}the knowledge of it is with Allah; He is the One who knows the exact time of its occurrence.{/idea} The verse says your Lord, speaking to the Prophet ﷺ, which brings closeness into a weighty subject.
now: Waiting for test results, a visa, a reply. Not knowing is hard. {reward}Some things are left with your Lord on purpose{/reward}, so your energy goes into today, not guessing.
old: Not knowing the future makes me anxious.
new: What I cannot know is held by my Lord, and that is enough.
try: Hand one unknown in your life to Allah in dua, then do today's work.

title: You are only a warner for those who fear it.
subtitle: The Prophet's ﷺ role
then: Ibn Kathir explains: I sent you {idea}to warn mankind and caution them{/idea}. Whoever fears Allah and standing before Him will follow you and succeed. Whoever denies you will only suffer loss.
now: A smoke alarm goes off. It does not tell you when the fire started or how big it is. {idea}Its job is to make you move.{/idea} The warning only helps the one who gets up.
old: I need all the details before I take a warning seriously.
new: A warning is meant to move me, not to satisfy my curiosity.
try: Act today on one warning from the Quran or Sunnah you have been putting off.

title: A whole life will feel like one afternoon.
subtitle: How short it will seem
then: Ibn Kathir says when they rise from their graves, {idea}the worldly life will seem only the afternoon of one day.{/idea} Ibn Abbas explained the afternoon as noon to sunset, and the morning as sunrise to noon. This is the last verse of the surah.
now: You look at an old school photo and think, where did those years go? It felt so long then. {reward}Your whole life will feel that way, one short afternoon.{/reward} Today is a big piece of it.
old: I have years and years ahead of me.
new: My whole life will feel like an afternoon, so this afternoon matters.
try: Spend this afternoon's first free ten minutes on something that will last.
